The shape edge vocabulary

“The styling on the rectangle primitives is not good. I think you are trying to combine both tldraw and excalidraw and figjam and it's not working.” Four asks came out of that: three fills, an edge colour that can differ from the fill, the line styles solid / dashed / dotted / async, and two connector weights. Then three more: the connector's row should be the rectangle's row with the labels off, the fill chips should run FigJam's way round, and switching between Transparent and No fill “seems buggy.” All of it is in, driven in a real browser, and on a review board. Read live from main / a9637fce (uncommitted edits present), 2026-09-05.

1 · Fill: FigJam's three, in FigJam's order — and painting what they say

tldraw ships none semi solid pattern fill lined-fill and the menu offered all six — the literal “three products at once” complaint. The vocabulary is FigJam's, so it stops at three, and runs FigJam's way round: most paint first. The colour popover lost 87px of width and the shape pill lost 60px with it.

SolidsolidTransparentsemiNo fillnone

The two that were the same white box

“It seems buggy as I switch between transparent and no fill.” The transitions were not buggy — all nine ordered pairs land on the right chip and the right stored value. What was wrong is what the two of them painted. tldraw resolves semi to the theme's flat canvas colour and solid to an 18% wash of the swatch, measured on a blue rectangle in the running app:

Solid, was#dcf0ff an 18% wash, not the blue you picked
Transparent, was#fcfffe the canvas colour, opaque — on a white board, No fill with extra steps
No fill— correct all along

On a white swatch all three collapsed into the same white box, and nothing about “Transparent” was transparent: it hid whatever it overlapped. The three now mean what the chips say, through the same display-values seam the edge colour uses — the swatch itself, the same colour at 25% so what is behind shows through, and nothing:

2 · Line style: the chips, and a palette of their own

This is the new capability, not just a shorter list. tldraw paints a shape's outline and its fill from one color, so “pale box, black edge” was unsayable. A shape's Line style is now FigJam's Stroke popover — the chips, a hairline, then an edge palette — behind the same three-bar trigger it always had. With no edge colour chosen the palette rings the shape's own colour, because that is what the outline is painted with.

SolidsolidDasheddashedDotteddottedAsyncasyncNonenone

None is kept although it wasn't in the four you named: without it a filled rectangle can't drop its border, and FigJam has it. Say the word and it goes.

3 · Async: the cable's own cadence, on a shape

The repo already had one async line — the cable's packet rail — so the shape reads from the same constant rather than a second opinion: 56 4 10 4 (56-unit carrier, 4-unit micro-gap, 10-unit packet, micro-gap), butt caps so the small gaps stay legible.

4 · The connector: the shape's own row, with the text off

Zach's rule for these menus: “the connector's little menu there should basically show the line styles from the rectangle. However, you toggle off the text.” That is now literally what it is — one control, one options list, one glyph set, and a layout that decides whether each option is named. Two lists is how they drifted in the first place: the connector's own Dotted icon was being drawn by the arrowhead renderer, because only the shape's control id reached the dash glyph. It rendered as a plain line.

ThinmThickxl

FigJam has two weights and now so does this. m rather than tldraw's s is bound to Thin on purpose: m is what every shape and cable is created at, so a cable drawn today reads as Thin instead of showing an empty row. The pair still spans a visible 3.5px→6px.

One vocabulary means one paint behind it, so the async cadence is a mixin over a stock ShapeUtil now (withAsyncEdge) rather than one shape's private trick: a rectangle, an arrow, a line and a freehand stroke all wear it. SVG restarts a dash pattern at each path and the cadence opens with a long painted carrier, so an arrowhead — its own short path — stays solid. A SystemSketch cable is the one connector this does not reach: its async is the Connection inspector's temporal control, which carries the packet semantics and the z⁻¹ pill rather than paint alone.

Where the two new facts live

Neither an edge colour nor async fits a stock style prop, and both are deliberately kept out of one:

FactStored asWhy not a style prop
Edge colourmeta.systemSketchStroke.color — a palette name A StyleProp only reaches shapes whose util declares it, and geo is tldraw's own shape. Adding a prop changes the on-disk schema of a stock record, so a .tldr written here would stop opening in plain tldraw.
async line style meta.systemSketchStroke.pattern, over a stored dash: solid PathBuilder.toSvg runs an exhaustive switch over the dash enum and throws on anything else, so addValues('async') would crash every shape drawn with it.

The paint comes back through tldraw's own seams: GeoShapeUtil.configure( {getCustomDisplayValues}) already exposes strokeColor and fillColor separately, and the async cadence is a CSS custom property on a display:contents wrapper for the canvas plus a <g> for the SVG export — both fed the same constant. Plain tldraw ignores the metadata and draws a solid outline, which is the whole point.

geo shape ├─ props.color ── fill, and the edge until one is chosen ├─ props.fill ── none | semi | solid ├─ props.dash ── solid | dashed | dotted | none (always a legal tldraw value) └─ meta.systemSketchStroke ├─ color ── the edge's own palette name (optional) └─ pattern ── "async" (optional)

Two smaller things that had to come with it

  • A fresh shape is drawn solid. tldraw's default dash is draw. With Draw gone from the menu, every new rectangle would have landed in a state its own menu couldn't express — so the mount seeds the next-shape dash, and only when the instance has none of its own, leaving a choice made on the canvas alone.
  • A stored value the menu no longer offers is named, not called “mixed”. A rectangle drawn before this holds draw; one shape with one definite value is not a mixed selection. The trigger says Line style, draw and the panel honestly checks nothing. The inspector gained the same honesty: it reports Line style: async and Edge colour beside the stock props, because an async shape's stored dash is solid.

Proof

  • npm run check — green: tsc, 1467 vitest tests, 118 Python tests.
  • npm run test:appearance — the real-browser journey, 21 passing steps. Its new one drives the whole gesture: open the Line style popover, assert the chips and palette, pick an edge colour and assert the painted stroke differs from the painted fill, pick Async and read 56 4 10 4 back out of the browser's computed style, then wait for the autosave and assert the file carries pattern: async beside a dash: solid plain tldraw can still draw.
  • 12 unit tests on the edge model itself — that clearing the last override drops the key entirely, that other metadata survives, that a text object in the selection doesn't make a rectangle read as mixed.

Decision surface

Done and proved

  • Fill is No fill / Transparent / Solid.
  • A shape's Line style is the chips over an edge palette; the edge colour is independent of the fill and survives save and reload.
  • async paints the cable's cadence on a shape, on canvas and in the SVG export.
  • Connector weight is Thin / Thick.

Deliberately not done

  • No custom hex on the edge — the 22nd “Custom” cell writes tldraw's own colour style, which is the fill's. The edge takes palette names only. Half a day to route the picker if you want it.
  • A cable's async stays in the Connection inspector — it means delivery, not paint, and it carries the z⁻¹ pill with it. The pill's Async is for stock arrows, lines, freehand strokes and shapes.

Needs you

  • Fixing Transparent repaints shapes you already have. Solid is now the swatch itself rather than an 18% wash of it, and Transparent is a 25% wash rather than near-white — your workspace has 400 shapes stored solid and 251 stored semi, and every one of them is bolder than it was this morning. It is the only way the three read apart on a white board, but the strength is one constant (TRANSPARENT_FILL_ALPHA) and the Solid mapping is one line. Default if you say nothing: both stay.
  • None in the line-style chips. You named four styles and none was None; I kept it because a filled rectangle otherwise can't drop its border, and FigJam has it. Default if you say nothing: it stays.
  • Whether the edge should follow the fill colour when you change the fill. Today, once you choose an edge colour it is pinned — FigJam's behaviour. Default if you say nothing: it stays pinned.
